newsitem.title: UK: LME metals lurch in thin pre-holiday activity.
newsitem.headline: LME metals lurch in thin pre-holiday activity.

text.p: Copper and nickel were pitched about in thin pre-market volume on Tuesday as trading wound down ahead of the Christmas holidays.
"Most everyone has already closed their books so any orders will move prices here and there," one trader said.
Copper chugged higher on speculative buying but ran out of steam ahead of LME inventory data which showed a rise of 3,950 tonnes, at the top end of expectations.
Three months prices dipped after the data but settled at $2,123/27 per tonne after a $2,130 kerb close on Monday.
Further support was pegged at $2,180, the low of December 16. Resistance was pegged at $2,150, then $2,175, Friday's high.
Nickel lost sight of the $6,500 level under the weight of light speculator selling, dipping to $6,465/85 after hitting 2-1/4 year lows on Monday.
Prices, however, recovered slightly and were last indicated at $6,490/$6,510 versus $6,515 at Monday's close.
Stocks rose by 150 tonnes, bringing the total to 49,548 tonnes, closer to the psychological 50,000 tonnne mark.
"If prices close below $6,500, we could see a major move lower, several hundred dollars," one trader said.

Chartist Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge said in a commentary "The immediate target remains $6,450 but we repeat that the longer-term possibility is a fall into the $6,000-$6,200 region."
Aluminium was sluggish even though stocks fell by 4,175 tonnes.
Prices were indicated at $1,554/55, up slightly from $1,550 on Monday, with the market seen trapped between support at $1,540 and resistance at $1,570.
Above $1,570, the next ceiling was seen in a band between $1,600 and $1,680, based on a congestion area of previous trade.
The others were barely changed with zinc indicated at $1,067/69 after $1,066 on Monday. Stocks fell by 1,950 tonnes.
Tin inventories rose by 270 tonnes and prices were at $5,780/795 versus $5,790.
Lead was a touch higher at $709/11 from $707 after stocks declined by 725 tonnes.
Alloy stocks dropped by 220 tonnes and the market was unchanged at $1,390/400.
